html:
The Ngurai-illam wurrung, also written Ngurelban or Ngurraiillam, are an Aboriginal Australian people of northern Victoria. Their country lay along the middle Goulburn River around today's Murchison, between the Taungurung upstream and the Yorta Yorta on the plains toward the Murray.

They lived from the river and its floodplain: fish, eels, waterbirds, and roots and seeds gathered by the women. Sources disagree on whether they were a people of their own or a clan close to the Taungurung.

Squatters took up runs along the Goulburn in the late 1830s, when this was still the Port Phillip District of New South Wales. Around 1840 a government protectorate station was set up near Murchison for the people of the area.
